This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, SVY02, fetched this session, places it in Santa Clara, California, and states 48 MW of flexible capacity in a single building on a 9 acre site, with 560,440 square feet of data hall space attributed on the page to that single building, labeled SVY02A in the facility own specification table. The page states the site was formerly the headquarters of the technology company Memorex, and is located minutes from San Jose International Airport. The page did not provide a street address or opening date.

reading.body:
The operator's own specification page for STACK SVY02 publishes one figure: 560,440 square feet of technical space. Megawatts of IT load, power density targets, and cooling architecture are not published. Without a power figure, no translation into racks or accelerators is possible, and this site will not invent one. The square footage alone is large, roughly the footprint of ten city blocks under roof, but physical area is not a proxy for AI capacity without knowing how that space is loaded.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so this site cannot characterize what compliance regimes the campus meets or what regulated workloads it qualifies to host.

California is the largest state in this site's data set by both facility count and published megawatts, with 103 mapped facilities and 170 MW of published IT capacity across 5 of those sites. SVY02 does not appear among the five facilities that have published a megawatt figure, which is why it carries no rank by power in the state summary. The campus is mapped, it is large by floor area, and it sits in Santa Clara County at the center of the densest AI infrastructure cluster in the country, but without a published power number it cannot yet be weighed against its neighbors.
